item.title: Davis Odd Fellows Thursday Live! — Thu Nov 5, 7:30 PM — Davis Odd Fellows
item.description:
Davis Odd Fellows Thursday Live! on November 5th presents Northern California’s King of Rockabilly, Mitch Polzak and The Royal Deuces. Thursday Live! is a monthly series of live music. Our shows are donation only. Your generous donations all go to the musicians. Our bar will be open. Mitch Polzak is a musician, guitarist, banjoist, singer, songwriter, and teacher. The 6’5” performer wears his heart on his sleeve and his playing from his heart. Polzak performs rockabilly and 60’s country music with the religious fervor of Jerry Lee Lewis and Johnny Cash and delivers a Honky Tonk ballad with the sincerity of Merle Haggard and Waylon Jennings. Mitch will bring a room to a fevered pitch of joyous energy on the dance floor and then tell you a story in a song like two old friends sitting at a kitchen table at midnight.

item.title: Out of Line: Art at the Edge — Fri Nov 6, 10:00 AM — Jan Shrem and Maria Manetti Shrem Museum of Art at UC Davis
item.description:
Inspired by conceptual artist Bruce Nauman’s video work “Dance or Exercise on the Perimeter of a Square (Square Dance), 1967–68,” this exhibition explores Davis as a site of both artistic practice and political protest. Mike Henderson, Ester Hernandez, Malaquías Montoya, Bruce Nauman, Nancy Rubins, Dorothy Wiley and the student artists of UC Davis’ Third World Forum engage with film, print and performance to confront who they were and what their work meant in a world of radical change. They made work wherever and however they could: in collaborative workshops, student newsrooms, kitchens and living rooms. While rooted in the politics of the late 20th century, “Out of Line” finds renewed meaning in the present day.
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Together Again, 1960–2026: Perspectives from UC Davis' Fine Arts Collection — Fri Nov 6, 10:00 AM — Jan Shrem and Maria Manetti Shrem Museum of Art at UC Davis
item.description:
This ongoing collection exhibition traces a history of art forged from this place. By focusing on relationships of many kinds, “Together Again” proposes that in order to understand an artwork in all its fullness, chance encounters and long-standing friendships often matter as much as formal affiliations. UC Davis legends such as Wayne Thiebaud, Deborah Butterfield and Bruce Nauman are exhibited alongside important regional voices that were once overlooked, and the exhibition extends to the artists shaping Northern California today, including Sadie Barnette, Woody De Othello and Ruby Neri.
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Above Bone — Fri Nov 6, 12:00 PM — Axis Gallery
item.description: ADERO WILLARD ABOVE BONE November 6–29, 2026 Reception and Artist Talk on Saturday, November 7, 5–8 PM Artist in the gallery on Sundays, November 8 and 29, 12–5 PM Axis Gallery presents Above Bone, an exhibition of ceramic sculpture by Sacramento artist Adero Willard, on view November 6 through 29, 2026. The exhibition brings together new work and pieces never before shown in Sacramento or on the West Coast. Join the artist for the reception and artist talk on Saturday, November 7, 5–8 PM. ABOUT THE EXHIBITION Above Bone refers to what is beneath, the layers, and what emerges. Clay sculptural vessels of heads and body forms explore death, regeneration, new growth, and what is hidden. Adero wrestles clay into expressive forms and creates surfaces dense in color and pattern: thick clay and delicately etched vines and flowers. item.title: Capturing Memories of Grief/Capturando Memorias del Duelo — Fri Nov 6, 12:00 PM — Axis Gallery
item.description: SUMMER VENTIS AND LINA RINCÓN CAPTURING MEMORIES OF GRIEF/CAPTURANDO MEMORIAS DEL DUELO November 6–29, 2026 Reception on Saturday, November 7, 5–8 PM The project, “Capturing Memories of Grief,” is a collaboration between artist Summer Ventis, sociologist and poet Lina Rincón, and you. Together, we explore the intersection of grief, memory, and image. We began this project with a conversation about our shared experience of losing a parent. When we recalled these experiences, we learned that we both had memories that centered around images, photographs, and the process of photography as a way to make sense of and process the meanings of our loss. In Fall of 2025, we began a series of grief-themed tours of works in the Crocker Art Museum’s collection. At the end of the tours, participants gathered to share and document our memories of grief and loss and how they connect with different types of images. item.description: This presentation brings together Catherine Hatzakos, Continuing Lecturer in the Writing Center, and Matthew Conner, Arts, Humanities, and Social Sciences Librarian, to discuss tools, pedagogies, and learning outcomes for teaching about disinformation. Register here 2026-2027 marks the UC Davis Campus Community Book Project’s 25th anniversary, and our theme—civil liberties—leans into the Book Project’s legacy of promoting dialogue and engaging diverse perspectives and audiences. item.title: Weekly Game Night at Blue Note — Wed Jan 20, 5:00 PM
item.description:
Yolo County Board Game Gathering Update 8/14/25: **We're still active**, but we primarily use Discord to chat and plan events. (See group description for invite link.)
We still meet every Wednesday for board games at Blue Note Brewing Company. We'll have a handful of tables reserved near the back; just look for the pile of board games.
People usually start arriving around 5pm, and games start whenever people are ready. Blue Note closes at 9pm, and although we have a 5-10 minute grace period there, you should be in the process of final scoring by 9, or else pack it up and play again another day.
Game night is open to all ages! Blue Note is a brewery, not a bar, so there's no restriction against minors. In addition to their crafted-in-house beer selection, water and sodas are available.

item.title: DataLab Office Hours (in person) — Tue Feb 2, 1:00 PM — Shields Library
item.description:
DataLab offers free in person drop-in office hours during which UC Davis researchers can obtain data science help and advice on working with their data. During these short, just-in-time sessions we meet with faculty, students, postdoctoral scholars, and staff from all domains across the University. Depending on the nature of your question and our availability, it may be possible to schedule a longer follow-up consultation after your office hours visit.
Appointments are not required. Please complete the brief office hours intake form ahead of time to help us connect you with the right expert for your question.
Common office hours help topics include:
Open Source Programming (R, Python, Julia, etc.)Reproducible research computing and data scienceResponsible and ethical data scienceData gathering, organization, databases, and experimental designData analysis, statistics, and explorationData visualizationMachine learning and neural networksText mining and natural language processingGeos

item.title: Out of Line: Art at the Edge — Thu Nov 5, 10:00 AM — Jan Shrem and Maria Manetti Shrem Museum of Art at UC Davis
item.description:
Inspired by conceptual artist Bruce Nauman’s video work “Dance or Exercise on the Perimeter of a Square (Square Dance), 1967–68,” this exhibition explores Davis as a site of both artistic practice and political protest. Mike Henderson, Ester Hernandez, Malaquías Montoya, Bruce Nauman, Nancy Rubins, Dorothy Wiley and the student artists of UC Davis’ Third World Forum engage with film, print and performance to confront who they were and what their work meant in a world of radical change. They made work wherever and however they could: in collaborative workshops, student newsrooms, kitchens and living rooms. While rooted in the politics of the late 20th century, “Out of Line” finds renewed meaning in the present day.
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Together Again, 1960–2026: Perspectives from UC Davis' Fine Arts Collection — Thu Nov 5, 10:00 AM — Jan Shrem and Maria Manetti Shrem Museum of Art at UC Davis
item.description:
This ongoing collection exhibition traces a history of art forged from this place. By focusing on relationships of many kinds, “Together Again” proposes that in order to understand an artwork in all its fullness, chance encounters and long-standing friendships often matter as much as formal affiliations. UC Davis legends such as Wayne Thiebaud, Deborah Butterfield and Bruce Nauman are exhibited alongside important regional voices that were once overlooked, and the exhibition extends to the artists shaping Northern California today, including Sadie Barnette, Woody De Othello and Ruby Neri.
Source: The Dirt
